messages.subject: Problem with  "geom_bar" & "scale_fill_manual"
parts:
hi all,

I need to plot a faceted plot and assign custom colors to each "ecommerce" in my plot. But the blogs and tuts on this are not very clear to me.

Thus I need your help.

My df has 3 columns: "ecommerce", "rangos", "cantidad".

I'll post the data as a txt file.

=============================================

This is the error I get:

Error in grDevices::col2rgb(colour, TRUE) : 
  invalid color name 'ecommercecolors'

=============================================

Code:

ggplot(tvs.rangos, aes(x = rangos, y = cantidad)) +
        
        geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "ecommercecolors") + 
        scale_colour_manual("ecommercecolors",
                values = c("linio" = "orange","ripley" = "blue","falabella" = "green")) +
        labs(title = "Marcas de TV por rangos de precios",
             x = "rangos de precios", y = "cantidad de tvs") +
        facet_wrap(~ ecommerce, nrow = 3) +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(colour="grey10",size=16,hjust=.5,vjust=.5,face="bold"),
              axis.text.y = element_text(colour="grey10",size=18,,hjust=1,vjust=0,face="plain"),  
              axis.title.x = element_text(colour="grey40",size=16,angle=0,hjust=.5,vjust=0,face="plain"),
              axis.title.y = element_text(colour="grey40",size=16,angle=90,hjust=.5,vjust=.5,face="plain"),
              plot.title = element_text(size = 18,vjust=4),
              legend.title = element_text(colour="grey40", size=16, face="bold"),
              legend.text = element_text(colour="grey10", size=16, face="bold"),
              strip.text.x = element_text(size = 20, angle = 0))

messages.subject: Re: Problem with "geom_bar" & "scale_fill_manual"
parts:
Hi:

The first reason why you got no response was because your dput
triggered an error when read into R:

> tv.rangos <- structure(list(ecommerce = structure(c(3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 1L,
+ 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L), .Label = c("linio",
+ "ripley", "falabella"), class = c("ordered", "factor")), rangos =
structure(c(2L,
+ 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L
+ ), .Label = c("< S/.500", "S/.500 - S/.1500", "S/.1500 - S/.2500",
+ "S/.2500 - S/.3500", "S/.3500 - S/.4500", "> S/.4,500"), class = c("ordered",
+ "factor")), cantidad = c(6L, 16L, 9L, 6L, 13L, 6L, 114L, 87L,
+ 44L, 33L, 39L, 1L, 17L, 21L, 8L, 8L, 24L)), row.names = c(NA,
+ -17L), vars = list(ecommerce), drop = TRUE, .Names = c("ecommerce",
+ "rangos", "cantidad"), class = c("grouped_df", "tbl_df", "tbl",
+ "data.frame"))
Error in structure(list(ecommerce = structure(c(3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 1L, :
object 'ecommerce' not found

The culprit appears to be the code "vars = list(ecommerce)", which
must exist in your session but wasn't exported. After removing the
code between 'vars =' up to 'class =', I managed to get something that
was workable. Hint: check that your data and code don't trigger
irrelevant errors in a fresh R session before sending it to a help
list.

Secondly, there are two reasons why you got the error in the ggplot()
call: (i) you didn't map the fill aesthetic to one of your variables
(you set it to a character string instead); (ii) there is no variable
named ecommercecolors in your data. Since you're only using one geom,
you may as well map the fill aesthetic in the ggplot() call.

Other edits:

* you used scale_colour_manual() when you meant to use
scale_fill_manual() (a common mistake);
* I split the legend title over two lines to give more space to the
actual charts;
* your x-labels ran all over each other in the bar chart, so I flipped
the axes to make the labels more readable.

This is what worked for me (R-3.2.3, ggplot2-2.0.0):

library(ggplot2)

tv.rangos <- structure(list(ecommerce = structure(c(3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 1L,
1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L), .Label = c("linio",
"ripley", "falabella"), class = c("ordered", "factor")), rangos =
structure(c(2L,
3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L
), .Label = c("< S/.500", "S/.500 - S/.1500", "S/.1500 - S/.2500",
"S/.2500 - S/.3500", "S/.3500 - S/.4500", "> S/.4,500"), class = c("ordered",
"factor")), cantidad = c(6L, 16L, 9L, 6L, 13L, 6L, 114L, 87L,
44L, 33L, 39L, 1L, 17L, 21L, 8L, 8L, 24L)), row.names = c(NA,
-17L), class = c("grouped_df", "tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame"))


ggplot(tv.rangos, aes(x = rangos, y = cantidad, fill = ecommerce)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
scale_fill_manual("ecommerce\ncolors",

values = c("linio" = "orange","ripley" =
"blue","falabella" = "green")) +
labs(title = "Marcas de TV por rangos de precios",
x = "rangos de precios", y = "cantidad de tvs") +
facet_wrap(~ ecommerce, nrow = 3) +

theme(axis.text.x =
element_text(colour="grey10",size=16,hjust=.5,vjust=.5,face="bold"),
axis.text.y =
element_text(colour="grey10",size=18,,hjust=1,vjust=0,face="plain"),
axis.title.x =
element_text(colour="grey40",size=16,angle=0,hjust=.5,vjust=0,face="plain"),
axis.title.y =
element_text(colour="grey40",size=16,angle=90,hjust=.5,vjust=.5,face="plain"),
plot.title = element_text(size = 18,vjust=4),
legend.title = element_text(colour="grey40", size=16,
face="bold"),
legend.text = element_text(colour="grey10", size=16, face="bold"),
strip.text.x = element_text(size = 20, angle = 0))

Hi Dennis, happy new year. 

Thank you very much for your effort. I got the result I was expecting. And it looks nicer with the coord_flip function applied on.

From your answer, I can see 2 mistakes from my part:

-I've used "fill" in the geom_bar function, instead of in the first call to ggplot function.
-I was using scale_colour_manual instead of scale_fill_manual.

Thanks again for your time.
